introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 2 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: three hours.**

Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. Mathematical formulae and tables published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The sequences $(u_n)$, $(v_n)$ and $(w_n)$ are defined by

$$\begin{cases} u_0 = -6 \\ u_{n+1} = \tfrac13\,(u_n - 2v_n) \end{cases} \quad\text{and}\quad \begin{cases} v_0 = 1 \\ v_{n+1} = \tfrac12\,(u_n + 3v_n) \end{cases}$$

$$w_n = u_n + v_n.$$
incertitudes: Question 10 : les définitions des suites, imprimées une seule fois, sont placées dans l'introduction commune de l'exercice ; les sous-questions sont notées i à vii. Le sujet imprime (vii) avec la somme de r = 0 à l'infini de (u_r - 14), indice r lu avec difficulté sur le scan ; la lecture retenue est cohérente avec la suite (iv).

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that $(w_n)$ is a geometric progression and give its $n$th term in terms of $n$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Using the definitions of $u_{n+1}$ and $v_{n+1}$:

$$w_{n+1} = u_{n+1} + v_{n+1} = \tfrac13(u_n - 2v_n) + \tfrac12(u_n + 3v_n) = \left(\tfrac13 + \tfrac12\right)u_n + \left(-\tfrac23 + \tfrac32\right)v_n = \tfrac56 u_n + \tfrac56 v_n = \tfrac56(u_n + v_n) = \tfrac56 w_n.$$

So $w_{n+1} = \tfrac56 w_n$ for every $n \ge 0$: $(w_n)$ is a geometric progression with common ratio $\tfrac56$. Its first term is $w_0 = u_0 + v_0 = -6 + 1 = -5$. Hence

$$\boxed{w_n = -5\left(\tfrac56\right)^n}.$$

(Check: $w_1 = u_1 + v_1 = -\tfrac83 - \tfrac32 = -\tfrac{25}{6} = -5\cdot\tfrac56$.)

$$u_{n+1} - u_n = \tfrac13(u_n - 2v_n) - u_n = \tfrac13(-2u_n - 2v_n) = -\tfrac23(u_n + v_n).$$

$$\boxed{u_{n+1} - u_n = -\tfrac23\,w_n}\qquad\left(= \tfrac{10}{3}\left(\tfrac56\right)^n \text{ by part (i)}\right).$$

Add the differences from $k = 0$ to $k = n - 1$ (the sum telescopes):

$$u_n - u_0 = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(u_{k+1} - u_k) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\tfrac{10}{3}\left(\tfrac56\right)^k = \tfrac{10}{3}\cdot\frac{1 - \left(\frac56\right)^n}{1 - \frac56} = \tfrac{10}{3}\cdot 6\left(1 - \left(\tfrac56\right)^n\right) = 20\left(1 - \left(\tfrac56\right)^n\right).$$

With $u_0 = -6$:

$$u_n = -6 + 20 - 20\left(\tfrac56\right)^n = \boxed{14 - 20\left(\tfrac56\right)^n}. \qquad\blacksquare$$

**Check.** $n = 0$: $14 - 20 = -6$. $n = 1$: $14 - \tfrac{50}{3} = -\tfrac83$, which equals $u_1 = \tfrac13(-6 - 2) = -\tfrac83$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Study the sense of variation (monotony) of $(u_n)$ and $(v_n)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sequence $(u_n)$.** By part (iii), $u_{n+1} - u_n = \tfrac{10}{3}\left(\tfrac56\right)^n > 0$ for every $n$. So $(u_n)$ is **strictly increasing**.

**Sequence $(v_n)$.** From $w_n = u_n + v_n$ and parts (i) and (iv):

$$v_n = w_n - u_n = -5\left(\tfrac56\right)^n - 14 + 20\left(\tfrac56\right)^n = 15\left(\tfrac56\right)^n - 14.$$

Then

$$v_{n+1} - v_n = 15\left(\tfrac56\right)^n\left(\tfrac56 - 1\right) = -\tfrac52\left(\tfrac56\right)^n < 0$$

for every $n$, so $(v_n)$ is **strictly decreasing**.

(Check: $v_0 = 15 - 14 = 1$ and $v_1 = \tfrac{25}{2} - 14 = -\tfrac32 = \tfrac12(u_0 + 3v_0)$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the limit of $(u_n)$ and deduce the limit of $(v_n)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $\left(\tfrac56\right)^n \to 0$,

$$\lim_{n\to\infty} u_n = 14 - 20\times 0 = \boxed{14}.$$

By part (ii), $w_n \to 0$, so

$$\lim_{n\to\infty} v_n = \lim_{n\to\infty}(w_n - u_n) = 0 - 14 = \boxed{-14}.$$

(Consistent with $v_n = 15\left(\tfrac56\right)^n - 14 \to -14$. The two limits are also consistent with the monotony found in (v): $u_n$ increases towards $14$ from below, $v_n$ decreases towards $-14$.)

From part (iv), $u_r - 14 = -20\left(\tfrac56\right)^r$. This is a geometric series with first term $-20$ and common ratio $\tfrac56$, and $\left|\tfrac56\right| < 1$, so it converges:

$$\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(u_r - 14) = -20\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\left(\tfrac56\right)^r = \frac{-20}{1 - \frac56} = -20\times 6 = \boxed{-120}.$$
